question: Should memory-lancedb autoCapture reject OpenClaw external-content wrappers by default, or should users opt into that behavior through a new captureFilter config surface?
rationale: The source-level gap is real, but the permanent fix sets a security default, config surface, plugin compatibility expectation, and operator opt-out story that automation should not choose alone.

options.title: Reject wrappers by default
options.body: Treat EXTERNAL_UNTRUSTED_CONTENT as a host-owned capture boundary before shouldCapture and add regression coverage for wrapped web/browser/cron-style content.

options.title: Add captureFilter config
options.body: Introduce excludeWrapped-style config with schema, manifest, docs, and tests while preserving current autoCapture defaults for existing users.

options.title: Defer to provenance design
options.body: Keep the narrow issue open until the broader memory trust/provenance model defines the canonical source-authority contract.

recommendation.title: Reject wrappers by default
recommendation.body: Treat EXTERNAL_UNTRUSTED_CONTENT as a host-owned capture boundary before shouldCapture and add regression coverage for wrapped web/browser/cron-style content.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice crosses external-content security boundaries and memory persistence behavior, and vincentkoc has recent history in both adjacent areas.
